The claim is architectural: visual consciousness may assign scale per scene-frame, building a world within the world.

Imagine sitting quietly in your living room when several tiny people walk across the floor. They are not vague shadows at the edge of your vision or fleeting shapes that disappear when you turn your head. They have bodies, clothing, faces, and an apparent purpose. Some may be accompanied by miniature animals or objects. They move through the same room you occupy, yet somehow they seem to belong to a world operating at a different scale. The natural reaction is to wonder what could make someone see such a thing, but there is another question hiding inside the experience that may be far more interesting. How does the mind know how to build the little world in the first place?

These experiences have a name: Lilliputian hallucinations, after the miniature inhabitants of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels. They have appeared in the medical literature for more than a century and have been associated with many different conditions, including vision loss, neurological disease, psychiatric disorders, and intoxication. They are not confined to one culture, one disease, or one drug. In many cases, the people experiencing them retain insight and understand that the figures cannot actually be present. Yet the figures nevertheless appear to occupy ordinary three-dimensional space, sometimes walking around the person's real surroundings as though they belong there.

French psychiatrist Raoul Leroy was studying these experiences in the early twentieth century, and by 1922, he was describing something more interesting than people simply seeing miniature humans. The little people could be accompanied by little animals and objects that were relatively proportionate to one another, and Leroy described this miniature world as moving and acting in relief and perspective. A few years later, psychiatrist Marion C. Alexander similarly wrote about little men, little horses, and other animals that were relatively proportioned. Importantly, she distinguished these experiences from micropsia, a perceptual disturbance in which things that actually exist simply appear smaller than they really are.

That distinction opens an entirely different scientific question. Suppose you look around your kitchen and everything appears half its normal size. The refrigerator is smaller, the table is smaller, your hands are smaller, and the person standing beside you is smaller. Something has apparently gone wrong with the visual system's calculation of scale, but there is still only one scale operating across the scene. Now imagine something different. The refrigerator remains normal, the table remains normal, and your hands remain normal, but a six-inch person walks across the table beside objects that are appropriately sized for that little person. The ordinary world has not simply shrunk. Something has apparently been generated inside it according to another set of dimensions.

A 2021 systematic review by psychiatrist Jan Dirk Blom assembled 226 published descriptions of Lilliputian hallucinations and showed just how widespread the phenomenon is. Ninety-seven percent of the hallucinations were experienced as grounded in the person's actual environment. Tiny animals appeared in 28 percent of the cases, mostly in addition to human figures, while accessory objects such as bicycles, carriages, musical instruments, and mechanical devices appeared in 15 percent. Blom described those accessories as equally minute and well-proportioned. That last observation is where this strange medical curiosity begins turning into a problem about the architecture of consciousness.

A tiny person by itself tells us that the brain can generate an image at an unusual scale. A tiny person with an appropriately sized bicycle tells us something more. A bicycle has dimensions that matter in relation to a human body. The seat, pedals, and handlebars cannot simply be assigned random sizes if the resulting scene is going to appear coherent. The same is true of a carriage and its passengers, a musician and an instrument, or a person and an animal. If these things appear together and remain proportionate, then the brain may not simply be generating several small objects independently. It may be constructing relationships among them.

One remarkable example was reported by Perret in 1923 and later discussed by Blom. The patient saw a tiny version of himself sitting in a horse-drawn carriage with his equally tiny mother. There is a great deal packed into that peculiar little scene. The brain generated two recognizable people and a vehicle, placed them together and assigned them a compatible miniature scale. Whether the carriage was perfectly proportioned in every geometric detail was not measured, because physicians in 1923 were not asking that question, but the report is enough to show why the question deserves to be asked now.

For most of the history of hallucination research, physicians were interested in sensible clinical questions. What did the patient see? Did the patient know it was unreal? Was the experience frightening or pleasant? Did it occur during intoxication, neurological disease, psychiatric illness or loss of vision? Those questions created a large literature describing the contents and causes of hallucinations, but they left another problem largely untouched. Very few researchers were asking about the metric rules governing the generated scene itself.

That gives us a different way to investigate hallucinations. Instead of concentrating primarily on whether someone sees a little man, an animal or a carriage, we can ask how those things are spatially related. Were the person and carriage actually present at the same moment, or were they seen hours or days apart and later listed together in a clinical report? Did they share the same scale? Did that scale remain stable? Did the ordinary room remain normal-sized? Did real objects block the hallucinated figures from view? If someone walked between the observer and a miniature figure, did the figure disappear appropriately behind the person? If the observer moved closer, did the apparent size change as it should for an object occupying three-dimensional space? If the observer looked away and returned, was the same scene still there?

These are not questions about whether the hallucinated beings are real. They are questions about how a conscious perceptual system constructs something that appears real. That distinction is essential because it allows the idea to be tested and, if the evidence does not support it, rejected. Perhaps the old clinical reports will turn out to contain mostly isolated miniature figures rather than coherent miniature scenes. Perhaps people saw tiny humans during one episode and tiny animals during another, while later summaries inadvertently made them sound simultaneous. Perhaps the apparent proportions are inconsistent. Perhaps the surrounding room sometimes shrinks along with everything else, making the experience closer to ordinary micropsia than to a separately generated scene. Any of those findings would weaken the stronger hypothesis.

If the opposite pattern appears, however, something much more interesting is happening. If the ordinary room repeatedly retains its normal scale while generated humans, animals, and objects share another internally coherent scale, consciousness may be capable of maintaining different metric organizations within a single perceptual experience. That would not tell us why the hallucination occurs or what ultimately causes the particular figures to appear, but it would tell us something about the machinery that constructs experienced space.

One unusual mushroom may eventually provide researchers with an opportunity to investigate this phenomenon prospectively instead of depending entirely on old case reports. Lanmaoa asiatica is a bolete eaten in Yunnan, China, and also reported from the northern Philippines. Properly cooked, it is consumed as food. When undercooked, however, it has become notorious for delayed hallucinations involving miniature human figures. The active substance responsible for the effect remains unidentified, and recent genomic work has not revealed the familiar psilocybin biosynthetic pathway that would provide an easy explanation.

The scientific value of Lanmaoa is not that it provides a portal into another world. It is that it may provide an unusual biological switch for a perceptual state that medicine has already documented from many unrelated causes. Instead of merely recording that an intoxicated patient saw little people, researchers could ask questions specifically designed to reveal how those people are being constructed in perceptual space. Viewing distance could be changed. Real objects could be placed between the observer and the hallucinated figure. Surfaces could be moved. The observer could look away and return. Relative dimensions could be estimated. Researchers could ask whether generated objects remain proportionate to generated agents and whether the surrounding room retains its ordinary scale.

Once those questions are asked, the little people almost become secondary to the experiment. What is really being investigated is the machinery that gives conscious experience its spatial structure. Under ordinary circumstances, that machinery works so effortlessly that we rarely notice it. We open our eyes and experience a room containing objects of stable sizes at apparently stable distances. A person walking toward us does not seem to double in physical size even though the image projected onto the retina grows dramatically larger. Chairs remain chairs as we move around them. Walls retain their dimensions. Objects disappear behind one another and reappear where they should. The brain continuously reconciles distance, perspective, scale, depth, motion, and occlusion, and consciousness receives the finished world without access to most of the calculations required to construct it.

Hallucinations may sometimes expose pieces of that machinery precisely because something unusual has happened to it. The scientific opportunity is therefore not simply to catalogue the strange things people see, but to use those experiences to determine which rules the perceptual system is capable of applying independently. A generated person might reveal one process. A generated person accompanied by a proportionately generated horse or carriage reveals another. A miniature population moving through a normally scaled room may reveal something more fundamental still about how scale is assigned inside conscious perception.

Psychiatry has known for roughly a century that people can experience proportionate miniature worlds. Modern systematic reviews have confirmed that Lilliputian hallucinations occur across different diagnoses and causes. What has not been systematically tested is the geometry of those worlds: whether generated objects reliably share an internal metric, whether that metric remains stable, and how it relates to the sensory geometry of the ordinary environment that may remain visible at the same time. That leaves us with a deceptively simple question. When consciousness generates a little person, how does it know how big that person's horse should be?

titles.title: Bayesian reaction optimization with fixed MaleCNS features: performance, wiring controls, and reward-aversion diagnostics — reproduction materials v31

descriptions.description:
All-version concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22695268. This version: 10.5281/zenodo.22739281.
Reproduction materials for Yuuya Nagata's exploratory study of Bayesian reaction optimization with fixed MaleCNS-derived mushroom-body features. The principal v26 predictive comparison and v27 response diagnostics are included alongside historical studies. v31 clarifies methodological comparisons and numerical provenance; it adds no new performance trajectories.
Start with MaleCNS_public_reproduction_v31.zip. This complete package contains the LaTeX/BibTeX8 paper and SI, original code, frozen protocols and selections, aggregate results, scientific figures, checksum-verifying importers, and 2,571 derived circuit/model files (539,985,407 bytes). Original MaleCNS tables and the C–N and Suzuki reaction databases are external inputs. Individual response histories, publisher PDFs and internal review correspondence are excluded from the v31 ZIP. Follow REPRODUCE.md for reproduction commands and limitations.
The exact original Docker policy image remains available from the earlier release 10.5281/zenodo.22695269. The present release does not establish superiority over development-tuned GP optimization, statistical equivalence, or a unique advantage of native connectivity.
License scope: CC BY 4.0 covers Yuuya Nagata's manuscript, original figures and aggregate results. Original project software is MIT; MaleCNS-derived materials and third-party components retain their licenses and attributions. The record-level license does not relicense those components. See LICENSE_SCOPE.md inside the v31 package.
Files include preparation-time validation snapshots. DOI reservation and local ZIP construction preceded publication; check this record for current access status.

Sole author: Yuuya Nagata. No funding was received; no acknowledgements or conflicts of interest. The v31 package excludes raw reaction/connectome databases and response-containing trajectories. Reproduction uses external source inputs and the original runtime identified in the previous release.

titles.title: Structure without semantics: derived cohort, analysis code and results ledger

descriptions.description:
Code, derived cohort and complete results ledger for a study testing whether the semantic content of feature groups drives performance in group-aware tabular transformers. The matched permutation control is run on eight datasets: a chronic kidney disease benchmark built so that the outcome-defining variables can be excluded, and seven public tabular datasets. Across 636 stored runs, semantically meaningful groups perform no better than randomly permuted groups of the same sizes; none of 28 dataset-metric comparisons reaches significance, and random-effects meta-analysis excludes any benefit above roughly 0.005 macro F1. No group count from one to sixteen separates from another. A companion analysis quantifies how supplying the variables that define the outcome inflates apparent accuracy and reorders model rankings. The ledger retains superseded results alongside their replacements so that seven reversals recorded during the study can be independently audited.

Changes in version 1.4.2

1. replication/yard_analyse.py wrote yardstick.json by zipping the computed equivalent_features values against a dataset-label list that applied a weaker filter than the one used to build the values: labels were filtered on membership in cost, values on cost greater than zero. Six labels were zipped against four values, silently mislabelling three of the four entries. The value belonging to heart-statlog was stored under credit-g, nursery's under heart-statlog, and sick's under mushroom. The script now derives the labels with the same positivity filter and asserts that the two lists are the same length.

The reported median of 0.93 equivalent features and the range 0.47 to 1.78 are computed from the correctly filtered value list and are unchanged. The console output was always correct. Only the JSON labels were wrong, and no number in the article was affected.

2. results/yardstick.json regenerated with correct labels.

No other code, stored run or reported number changes in this version.

Changes in version 1.4.1

1. README.md cited DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22647492 (v1.3.0) in its Citations section. Corrected to this version's DOI, with the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22209017 noted for citing all versions.

2. CITATION.cff carried no DOI field. The version DOI and the concept DOI are now both recorded.

No code, no stored run, no reported number and no data file changes in this version.

Changes in version 1.4.0

Made in response to editorial checks by PeerJ Computer Science.

1. The 26 predicted-probability arrays stored as .npy are now accompanied by .csv equivalents of the same data, so that every stored result is readable without NumPy. The .npy files are retained because the figure scripts load them directly.

2. README.md has been rewritten to the structure required for AI Application articles: title, description, dataset information, code information, usage instructions, requirements, methodology, citations, and licence with contribution guidelines.

3. CITATION.cff version and date updated.

No code, no stored run and no reported number changes in this version. The analyses and figures reproduce exactly as in v1.3.0.

Changes in version 1.3.0

This version corrects three reproducibility defects in v1.2.0.

1. The stored predicted-probability arrays that the figure scripts read were missing from the archive, so those scripts could not be run. All 26 arrays are now included, and the three scripts have been verified to reproduce all five published figures pixel-for-pixel from a clean extraction.

2. figures.py and fig4_new.py both wrote fig3_riskcoverage.png, so run order silently determined which figure survived. The obsolete block is disabled, and the filename-to-figure mapping and run order are documented in MANIFEST.md.

3. split_meta.json could not be regenerated by any script in v1.2.0. The split-averaged meta-analysis has been rewritten as split_meta.py and recomputed from the stored runs. The pooled estimate changes from -0.0022 (95% CI [-0.0083, +0.0038]) to -0.0011 (95% CI [-0.0072, +0.0051]), and the bound on any benefit from semantic grouping from 0.004 to 0.005 macro F1. The conclusion is unchanged. This is recorded as the seventh reversal in the study.

Figures now render at 450 dpi and carry no titles inside the image files.

This repository contains the datasets and statistical analysis files supporting the study on the cultivation of Lentinula edodes using alternative agricultural substrates.

The dataset includes raw experimental data from agronomic evaluations (yield, biological efficiency, number and weight of mushrooms, and precocity), mushroom proximate composition, and the R scripts used for statistical analyses.

titles.title: Phenotypic image dataset of naturally grown shiitake mushrooms across multiple varieties and growth stages

descriptions.description: This dataset contains phenotypic images of naturally grown shiitake mushrooms collected under real cultivation conditions. The dataset covers multiple shiitake mushroom varieties and growth stages and supports classification, grading, and object detection tasks. The dataset includes RGB images acquired in natural cultivation environments with varying illumination conditions, occlusions, overlaps, and complex backgrounds. Corresponding object detection annotations are provided as plain-text label files compatible with mainstream deep learning detection frameworks. The dataset was developed to support research in agricultural computer vision, intelligent mushroom cultivation, phenotypic analysis, and deep learning-based detection methods. The repository contains image data, annotation files, metadata, and related scripts for dataset organization and experimental reproduction used in the accompanying manuscript.

titles.title: Tyrosinase Inhibitors Dataset: 1725 Compounds with Experimental IC50 Values from ChEMBL and BindingDB

descriptions.description:
This dataset contains 1,725 curated tyrosinase inhibitors with experimental IC50 values collected from ChEMBL (v34) and BindingDB databases. The dataset includes compounds tested against mushroom tyrosinase (Agaricus bisporus, CHEMBL3318) and human tyrosinase (CHEMBL1973).

Each entry contains:- SMILES structure- IC50 (nM and µM)- pIC50- Molecular descriptors (MW, LogP, HBD, HBA, TPSA, RotBonds)- Lipinski Rule of 5 compliance- Data source (ChEMBL/BindingDB)

Dataset statistics:- Total compounds: 1,725- Lipinski compliant: 83.4%- IC50 < 1 µM: 826 compounds- IC50 < 100 nM: 598 compounds

This dataset is intended for machine learning and QSAR modeling applications in tyrosinase inhibitor discovery.

titles.title: Guanyin on a Dragon Throne at The Royal Ontario Museum, Ontario

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 4.0 International

descriptions.description: This sandstone and polychrome, large sculpture depicts Guanyin on a dragon throne. It originates from the 14th-15th Century (Ming dynasty) and was made in the Shanxi Province.  The seated bodhisattva Guanyin is recognizable by the small image of Amitabha Buddha in his crown. The rocks which flank Guanyin are home to nine animals, including a goat, an elephant, a monkey, a snake, a dragon, a lion and a deer with the mushroom of immortality. At the deity's feet are two standing figures with hats (possibly donors), two small bodhisattvas, and a large dragon.     This object is part of Scan The World. Scan the World is a non-profit initiative introduced by MyMiniFactory, through which we are creating a digital archive of fully 3D printable sculptures, artworks and landmarks from across the globe for the public to access for free. Scan the World is an open source, community effort, if you have interesting items around you and would like to contribute, email stw@myminifactory.com to find out how you can help.

descriptions.description:
Chasing Crows ByVoight KampffThis road had been longer than the memory could recall, he hated it.It had morphed from motorway to road, to track and now to narrow path. It dissolved into nothing but a lonesome tree, this was no oasis nor the foot of a castle but a meaningless nothing, not even the rotting corpse of the last sorry wretch that must have trod the last of this path, an empty desert, this was the end of things, freedom is not so pretty a word for those who make it this far."A million and one places you could have stopped, what twist of madness drove you to leave your bones here?"

 

 

 

Kappa swung his axe without the force to split this last log and decided not to bother his arse pulling it out for another swing "fuck it", he collected up as much wood as he could wrap his arms around and went inside.This was the edge of the world where forests and mountains don't have names, Kappa hadn't assigned them with names, they were memories."Smelly, damp, up to your neck in brambles wood" or "Fuck that, I’m not going up there again mountain".Kappa hadn't seen a single soul in these parts and had decided long ago, that might be for the best.Out of ear shot and further than the eye can see, this was his kingdom, a small roughly made home in a small untidy clearing surrounded by quiet.Kappa, who on any other occasion might be strutting around naked, singing badly, throwing stones into the stream, was in a sombre mood.Kappa’s cheek had swollen, Kappa had had tooth ache for four days now and there was no sign of his immune system gaining a foothold on the rot.This was a great cause for concern, Kappa feared the descent into desperation and what that might mean, how far a thing will go to escape pain.Kappa had turned his home over trying to find an answer. It dawned on him long before peering into an old boot for the third time that this was no hunt for a pain relief, there wasn’t any, this was a failing exercise in distraction. “Fuck fuck fuck fuck” in time with the throbbing in his face.The clove would have kicked in by now if it was going too, a moan of desperation made it to his vocal chords as he knelt down in the middle of the floor and began to rock back and forth in a failing attempt to sooth away the noise in his head “What the fuck am I meant to do now?”“If you’re really out there, NOW is you BIG fucking chance, I am asking for your help, if you really exist, now would be an excellent time to help me the fuck out!”Kappa pauses for a deliberate and belligerently short couple of seconds “Didn’t think so you lousy fucker”.Kappa sprang to his feet, marched over to the sink, dragged his tool box from underneath and rummaged through it with a clatter.Kappa pulled out a hammer, looked at it and with a half chuckle half cry, dispensed with the idea of attempting to knock the offending tooth out with it, tossed it aside and clattered through his tool box some more, pulled out his pliers, old rusty and reluctant to open even with some force, held them up in the air and inspected them “shit!”.“I've been here before, you cant grip a tooth with pliers, the angles are all wrong and teeth, way too slippery”.Despite this, Kappa reached into his mouth with the pliers, gripped the tooth as best he could and gently moved them to see if the grip was good “aarrrr” in anticipation. The pain was no worse, the tooth moved with the pliers, the grip seemed good “aaaaaarrrrr” again in anticipation as he contemplated his next move, pulling was no good the pliers would slip off, the only other possible move was to twist it out in one aggressive move. “Aaaaaarrrrrrrrrrr”... The pliers snapped shut as they slipped off the tooth, the pain soared to new heights. Kappa slammed to the floor, curled up in a ball and began banging his forehead against his knees whilst singing a song with no distinguishable words, waiting for the pandemonium inside his head to ease.“This is fucked!..The nearest help is further than I can walk in a week”.Kappa jumped to his feet grabbed the torch from behind the door, lit it on the fire and stepped outside. Outside was dark and still with stars sprayed across the sky.It was cold enough to see the breath. On any other night Kappa might have pulled out his chair, lit a smoke and pondered the magnitude of existence but tonight Kappa strode off into the forest at a determined pace. Ten minutes later Kappa arrived into a small damp clearing, knelt down and began to scan the earth around him. His torch, still burning well, lit an orange dome of shadows, leaves and branches that leaned in and danced with the flame.Kappa was no big fan of the dark especially this far from his warm fire but the way he felt right now he'd Kick a rabid dog in the bollocks just to take him away from the here and now.“Ah there you are”, Kappa leaned in towards the ground and brought his torch forward, tucked under a tree root was a small grey blue mushroom.Kappa drew a deep breath, carefully reached out and plucked the mushroom from its hiding place, held it up to the light and inspected it.After another deep breath he carefully reached into his mouth and placed it between his cheek and his gum where the most pain was emanating.Kappa was momentarily statuesque in his orange dome waiting for the urgency of his mission to ebb and his here and now to catch up.

After a short pause Kappa begins to inspect his surroundings, the light of his torch does not reach far into the dark, not far enough to see any incoming claws or teeth.“Don't wind yourself up Kappa” he mutters to himself as he looks behind, then to the left, then right, then left, and then behind again. “Stay calm,” he whispers. Kappa knew there were no such things as monsters but he only knew this when the sun was up, now it was dark and he wasn't so sure. “Everything is fine,” he says a little louder in an attempt to convince himself that his voice won't wake anything with more teeth than brain cells.A piece of burning material that flakes from his torch and drops to the floor catches his attention, he looks at it and then at the torch.“Shit! That's not going to last ten minutes”, Kappa bolts into a march, resisting the urge to run but at this pace the torch starts to roar as it cuts through the air, Kappa feels that its making too much noise and he wont hear any teeth stalking him. “Shit!” he picks up the pace, the roar gets louder and he tries to look in all directions at once... THUNK! His foot snagged a root, like a noose and as strong as rope, it shows his foot no mercy. He lunges forward, his boots slapping the ground desperately trying to catch up with his head but it was too late. Kappa has to throw his arms forward to break his fall. Straight into a bramble, sparks flying every which way.Kappa jumped up in a flash ripping himself from the thorn's grip.Holding what was left of his the torch high above his head he begins to slowly rotate so he can scan in all directions. There’s no tooth ache here and he can't feel the blood running down from his elbow or the peppering from the brambles but he can hear his lungs heaving. His breathing is making too much noise he can't hear past it. He tries to hold his breath but it only makes him all the more desperate to heave great lungs of noisy air. Suddenly there's a sound in the brambles right next to him. Something moved. This triggers every muscle in his body to attempt a leap from this world into a better one, Kappa is now at full tilt, leaping fallen trees with barely a touch and dodging the whirlwind of obstacles that his pace is throwing at him.Kappa curses himself as his logic catches up. “It was the brambles springing back into position, idiot!” but it was too late he was unable to calm. His instincts and imagination had taken over and his logic was along for the ride. The oil on the hessian is all but used up and the torch is now leaving a trail of tiny fires as the hessian breaks up, each piece taking some of the all important light with it, “Fuck fuck fuck!” Kappa, who is no longer looking back allows his imagination to insert claws and teeth reaching out for his calves... Of course there wasn't but Kappa’s imagination was running as fast as he was and was going to run his feet to stumps until it knew for sure.“Fuck it, fuck it, fuck it!” The last of the torch flickers out. Kappa is nearing his home and knows the area like the back of his hand. He drops the dead torch and starts to use both hands to help propel him forward past the last of the trees. At last, he can see the glow of his fire through the shutters. He races across the clearing and slams through his door, digs his heels in on the other side and slams his weight back against the closing door. “Fuck it! Every fucking time!”.Kappa leans against the door heaving in and out, his brain trying to make sense of the gap between his logic and his response, his body still pinning the door shut.“The fucking brambles I landed in were just springing back after you crushed them, you fucking dumb-ass!”.Kappa starts to catch his breath and relax a little but still pauses for a moment before he lets go of the door. Now he feels the pain, the mushroom tastes earthy but the tooth ache is bearable.Kappa’s arms sting, he stands in the light of his fire and begins the task of removing thorns.Kappa chuckles at himself, "You dozy shite, I don’t believe you did that shit.”He continues to hunt for thorns on his body where he knows he has already removed them. “Fucking thorns, they feel just the same when you take them out.” The blood that had run from his elbow to his wrist had dried and was not helping.Kappa threw a couple of logs on the fire, rolled a smoke and slumped into his chair to absorb the warm orange glow, tonight the fire was extra warm and the glow extra orange. “Splendid.” Kappa drifted back into the tranquillity of meandering thought, the fire spat occasionally and had settled to a dull glow. Kappa closed his eyes and wondered what it might be like to swim in the cool blue ocean again. He knew it was out there somewhere, it was out there right now hissing against its bleached rocks and red sand. He wondered if someone was there right now appreciating it, absorbing it, he wanted to dip his toe, it left an ache in his heart.BANG BANG BANG!!!!“What the...!” Kappa’s body flails in shock.No one ever bangs on his door. In all the time Kappa had lived here no one but Kappa had even stood in his clearing.Kappa bolts upright facing the door his heart pounding in his ears and his eyes wide.“This is no springy bramble taking the piss, something is out there and it’s banging on my fucking door!”BANG BANG BANG! Kappa jumped again, “Who is it?”No answer, Kappa swoops up the hammer that was amongst the tools he had left strewn on the floor, but its not impressive, he wished it had been his axe but that was outside with whatever was banging on his door.Still no answer.BANG BANG BANG! Kappa recoils again, pauses for a moment then moves towards the door. He tries to get to the door before its struck again, he doesn't want to hear that banging ever again.BANG BANG BANG BANG!“For fucks sake!” A spark of anger this time.Kappa steps forward spurred on in the knowledge that he will get to the door before its struck again, he clenches the hammer, reaches out, grabs the latch and pulls the door open.More than filling the doorway is a shadow. From head to toe a bottomless black, the only visible part of this beast is the bony hand that's wrapped around a staff that's as long as the beast is tall.“Yes?” Kappa exclaims a little more feeble than he would have hoped.“Can I come in?” The voice rumbled like it had travelled through the earth, it sent nearby crows from their roost into the black air cawing their alarm as they escaped into the night.Kappa wanted to go with them but instead, here he was, trapped behind Mr Black, there was nowhere to run.Despite what his heart was pleading, Kappa stepped back from the door “Yes, come in.” Mr Black ducked his head and stepped through the door passed Kappa. As he did Kappa looked at the open door but before he could contemplate the pros and cons of chasing the crows, Mr Black turned to the door, took a deep breath and sighed.”You could but you would be out there, alone and in the dark, not knowing where I am or which tree I'll step from behind. It would be better to stay here where you can keep an eye on me, yes?”Kappa squirmed at the potency, this fucker seemed powerful and Kappa instantly felt the oppression of a shrew beneath the paw of a cat.Black took the box that Kappa had been using to rest his feet on in front of the fire, sat on it, stuck out his bony hands to warm then on the fire rubbing them together with a dry rasping sound.“You don’t mind do you, its a bit nippy out there tonight.”“Go right ahead” Kappa said.“Why don’t you take a seat?” Black gestured towards Kappa’s chair.Kappa reluctantly closed the door on his last chance to join the crows. His movements felt jerky and deliberate as they fought against the truth. He stepped past Black without taking his eyes from where he imagined Black's eyes would be if he could see them, and eased himself back into his chair. “You doing a bit of DIY Kappa?” Kappa had become unaware that he still had the hammer clenched tightly in his fist.Kappa, struggling to control his voice, croaked “Yeah sort of... You know my name?”Kappa slowly relaxed his grip and allowed the hammer to drop by the side of his chair, trying to picture exactly where it would be should he need it in an emergency.“You'd be amazed at some of the things I know, I know how far it is to madness and back, how many moons before despair gives way to surrender and how many strands of spider’s silk it would take to pull a tooth from a dead man’s head, do you know why I am here?”.Kappa thoughts spun, he knew something but he didn’t have the words or the heart to speak of such things.Kappa had always felt that he ought attempt to maintain a pinch of humour when faced with such impending doom. He had often pondered if he would have the gumption for such a sport in the real world.Kappa heaved against his instincts and crocked “Rag n Bone?” Black rumbled a chuckle like gravel.“Yes, very good Kappa, I'm the Rag n Bone man.” There was a long pause, Kappa squirmed and waited but the Rag n Bone man seemed done and was back to warming his hands on Kappa’s fire.The vacuum of silence filled with the violence of Kappas worst fears.His mind raced from notion to notion at lightning speed hunting for a way out, an entire lap of his mind and he found nothing. Kappa heaved at the air and tried to calm himself, "Fuck it, I'm being stalked." he thought, hiding when there's nowhere to hide is for pussies.Yeah, but I’m a pussy… Meow.Kappa took a deep breath and exclaimed in a whispered half statement half question kind of way “Your Death?” Black for the first time turned towards Kappa, there were still no eyes to see in the shadow of Blacks cloak."And you’re brave... When you want to be."“You're here to watch me die?!”“I am here to watch you over the river so to speak, not watch you die”. “I’m dead?”“Don’t let the fact that you are breathing in and out fool you Kappa. You’re about as dead as a thing needs to be for me to come knocking. It's been years, I would have come sooner but I've been a bit busy… you okay? Come on, let's make a move.”The Rag n Bone man stood and turned to the door.“It takes all that is left of me to keep from my knees and vomiting on your shoes, go where?”Kappa’s chest was starting to heave again.Black leaned forward and looked at his feet, “I'm not wearing any shoes? Come on, I need a drink”.“What?!” ”Can we not wait a bit? How about a nice cup of tea? Blackberry wine?Can we not go tomorrow when the sun comes up?" Kappa's voice was starting to plead, he felt he would need at least a couple of days to weigh this shit up but had the feeling he wouldn’t get it.He was right.“Kappa, we’ve got places to go.” Black stepped toward the door. Kappa, who to some small degree had grown accustomed to his guest, reluctantly pushed himself to his feet and turned to Black.“How bad is this all going to get?” “No one is going to stick needles in your eyes.”“Oh, that’s good!”“Listen Kappa, is it hurting right now?” "My bones are rattling under my skin." "Tell me when it hurts, until then let's roll.""But what’s wrong with being dead right here?""Kappa, your shit is in pretty good order, lets roll some bones and get on with it!"Black stepped outside and sets off towards the woods, taking huge strides. Kappa has to sporadically run, then walk, then run to keep up with him.Kappa took one last look to see where the crows had gone as they both stepped out of the clearing and into the dark.It's as dark as its ever been in the forest and Kappa is making sure he doesn’t lose sight of Black. He has to hold back a laugh.“This is fucking madness, I’m trying to keep up with Death because I feel safe next to you, if a beast jumps out of the shadows you will kick its ass!” Black stops suddenly and Kappa runs straight into the back of him and bounces off. “I'll bust a cap in his ass.” Black states in a shite American accent and blows the smoke from the end of his finger… Gunslinger style.Black abruptly strides off again.Kappa’s mind swirls without conclusion.“Where are we going?”“Why am I following this fucker?”“Who is this fucker?”“How much shit am I in this time?”Kappa eventually starts to tire and is falling back. He shouts to Black, “Slow down, I need a rest!” but Black has disappeared over a crest.Kappa is on the verge of panic and was thinking about changing his mind about liking the Rag n Bone man but when he topped the crest, there was Black sitting in a clearing next to a roaring campfire, smoking a pipe.This night was already way too absurd for this to seem particularly unusual. Kappa stepped into the clearing and sat next to the fire.“I didn't bring my backy, I somehow didn't think I was going to need it where we were going, where are we going?”Black reached into his cloak and pulled out a pouch and tossed it over to Kappa.“Where do you think were going?”“To see the Big Cheese, to get a god almighty bollocking for being such a useless piece of shite.”Kappa looked into the pouch trying to hide the sincerity of his speculation. “Err, any papers?”Black rummaged again and tossed Kappa some papers.“That’s a pretty dark take Kappa, if you were being optimistic then where would you think we we’re going?”“To see the Big Cheese to have some beers and talk endless amounts of shite laugh and laugh get pissed and have a kebab… Oh, and to be forgiven for being a useless piece of shite”“When was the last time you spoke to anybody Kappa?”Kappa stared off into infinity.“Dunno… Couple of years?... “ He looked down again to finish making his smoke trying his best to act as though all this shit was perfectly ordinary, his bones still rattling under his skin.“It's been seven years,” Black states. Kappa stared off again, tried to count the years in his head and abandons the attempt.“I've been busy.”“Doing what?“ ”Minding my own business.”Kappa reaches into the fire for a burning stick and lights his smoke.“Its the lesser of two evils… Don't get me wrong it's not what I dreamed of but it's the best I can do with what I've got and it's not all bad. I mean you should have tried some of that blackberry wine I've been working on, it doesn’t taste for shit but it’ll put a lovely warm glow in your cheeks.”Black looks at Kappa then back to the fire and shakes his head.“Sounds great, what was it you dreamed of?”“Dunno, just some silly shit.”“Go on then.”“Fuck that, its just some weird shit.”Black begins to shuffle, “Well, I guess we should make a move then.”“Fuck it, you win, I'll tell you, just let's hang on here a bit. I’m tired… besides, I’m not sure I want to get to where we’re going.”Black makes himself comfy again, taps the ash from his pipe and begins to re stuff it.“Okay, I dreamed that there be at least two of whatever it is that I am.”Black chuckles while lighting his pipe with a twig.“What went wrong?”“Bridging the gap, reaching out, laying my cards down.I didn’t fancy any of that shit.If anyone were to like me they would need to know me first and no fucker is rummaging around in my head!”Kappa drew deeply on his smoke.“I feared I had the blackest heart and the darkest corners, no one would ever accept this twisted knot of wrong.The noise of that immovable meeting the unstoppable proved a tad too noisy for my taste… Fuck it, I wasn’t ready for any of that shit, I would find something else to do instead.”“The unstoppable?”“Yeah, the truth in one hand and the desire to be accepted in the other, irreconcilable, times being what they are.”“Or maybe it was the inner vs the outer or me vs them, the dark vs the light, ying, yang and all that crazy jazz.”“What are you talking about Kappa?” Black rumbled.“Look, for as far as I can remember, my life has been the longest bollocking, don’t do this, stop doing that, put that down, pick that up, you need to do this and you need to think that, fuck it!Then some other lousy fucker is saying if you lie you only lie to yourself if you cheat you only cheat yourself. Okay I thought, I'll give being honest a go, fuck off and leave me alone. Either I'm not like you or you don't like yourself enough to like me, either way, go fuck yourself and leave me alone. You will only want to fix me and I'm not the one who needs fixing… Of course that's exactly what they wanted to do, fix me. I got so tired of being prodded and poked that I decided for the sake of quiet to keep my head down and fake being like everyone else. But there was a problem, before I knew it I had forgotten that I was faking. They got what they wanted. I was fixed, forget about there being two of what ever it is that I was, there were fucking millions of us. Millions of contortions, hiding, ducking and diving, staring across a huge divide at each other in as much pain as ever and not knowing why. Then something woke me and I started to remember all sorts of shit.”Black interrupted, “What woke you?”“I don’t know, the sky caved in, the immovable moved or the unstoppable stopped.”“Are you trying not to make sense?”“Don't take the piss Black, you know exactly what I mean, I had lost it. The tension got too much and something snapped.I saw all sorts of mad shit that made me want to run faster than I'd ever run before.” “What did you see?”"Fuck you Black!""What did you see Kappa?”“I said fuck you Black!”A long silence took its toll on Kappas anger, Kappa switched tone to a low mumble.“I stumbled across the Big Cheese face down in the gutter. He was there because of me, it was my fault. It broke my fucking heart. I had been blind and now I could fucking see it, I could see it fucking all!”“You put the Big Cheese in the gutter?”“I didn’t say that, I said the sky fell, something snapped and that’s what I saw. Why am I telling this shit? You might be powerful, in fact I bet you could knock my teeth through the back of my head. Maybe I should bow and scrape but that seems wrong for some reason. I’m really tempted to like you Black but you’re starting to get on my tits. If this whole episode is going to be nothing but pain then maybe you can fuck off and tell the Big Cheese that if he is the vandal that pulled me from the bliss of eternal nothingness just to replace it with all this rotten shite, then he can put me the fuck back and never disturb me again!”“You're doing it again Kappa, but my apologies all the same.”Kappa squirmed, “Maybe I should I take another one of those bollockings to go with my fear? I don’t need any apology.”“Okay, it's just that you talk about bridging the gap and still insist on ducking and diving… Oh and by the way, I know I look big but I’m all skin and bone, you could probably knock my teeth through the back of my head.”Kappa paused, then pointed into the dark. “You mean a mad axe man could step out of the forest and carve us to bits and you wouldn’t be able to stop him?!”“Well, no. He would take one look at us and slink away sharpish, mad axemen have imaginations too and we don’t exactly look like easy prey.”Kappa chuckled and leaned into the welcome distraction, he trusted Blacks point.Black breaks the tranquillity.“So, the Big Cheese was in the gutter.”Kappa reluctantly returns.“Yeah, somehow the world hadn’t been enough for me. The trees, the sky, bird song, babbling streams, no matter what he tried, it wasn’t enough to make me happy.He was pleading to know how such a thing might be done.I was mortified, no fucking way was I having someone crawl in the mud on my account!Anyway, I walked out of that episode naked. I was a fake, I felt as wrong as I have ever been. I took back the parts of me that I had given away and escaped. There wasn’t two of whatever it is that I was and now, I wasn’t sure there were millions of us either.I would look for the rain and the trees, the rainbows and rabbits. Elevate the world from a backdrop to my pain into an attempt to soar above thinking being born had been a mistake. I had an ethical motive to be extracting some joy from the world in any which way I could so the Big Cheese could escape the gutter… Fucking insanity when you think about it but I couldn’t shake it off, not all of it.”“There’s a word for that Kappa.”“Yep, insanity.”“No, not quite Kappa.”Kappa resisted enquiring.Kappa’s instincts told him how easy it is to be wrong, his memory told him how often he had been wrong and his heart told him he was tired.Tired of rebuilding, repairing then demolishing again.He liked the quiet of solitude, the mirror was not required in solitude.Black leaned back onto a log and drew on his pipe.“You decided to shun all people and live alone.” “I needed to lick my wounds, gather my thoughts and got used to the quiet.”“So you're done with the dream?”“I don't wish to resurrect the desire. Besides, living that dream means hiding from the truth or returning to the insanity of chanting “I want to go home,” while sitting at home.I lost the ability, so yeah, pretty much. It was sad when I thought about it but until you turned up things were pretty cool, I had a roof and a fire to ward off the cold, I had stuff to do, things to learn and trees to sit under.It was calm and quiet.What about you? Your dream?, did you have a dream?, do you have a dream?”Black shuffled,“Yeah, I dreamed there be two of whatever it is that I am.”Kappa snapped at Black “You’re really fucking funny Black, not only do you deliver shite news you tell shite jokes.”“You think so?”Kappa is hesitant to take Black seriously.“What is it that you are?”“I’m the Rag n Bone man Kappa.”“You are alone?”“Not right now I’m not”.Black drew deeply on his pipe and exhaled with satisfaction.Kappa struggled with the impasse.The silence is cold.“I've been dead for years?”“You wandered into the big empty.”“Surely I would have noticed.”“You did, that’s why you wandered into the desert. What was it that had you leave the comforts of home?”“I've already told you, I was at home chanting that I wanted to go home, over and over, something had broken, I needed to escape to somewhere and think”.“What about?”“Nothing, I needed to get away, I needed some quiet.”“From what?”“The fucking noise in my head!”“What was the noise!?”“The noise I am hearing right fucking now!”Kappa turned away from the fire in an attempt to blot it all out.It didn’t help.“For fucks sake Black, I was ashamed, ashamed at the magnitude of my misconception and ashamed of how short I fell from the designated line of acceptability. I told you, there was a gap between their acceptable and my honest, on top of that, every repair I tried to make crumbled in my hands.”“You’re doing it again, you’re speaking in code.”“And your fucking surprised?!”“If you can't decipher my code you're not worthy of its content. The code's there for a fucking reason!”“It's not like you killed someone Kappa!”Kappa paused for a while taking what small comfort he could from Black’s words, drew deeply on his smoke and continued on in his reluctant tone. “Bollocks... I was on a mission to make sure I was a decent, worthy human so that I didn’t have to look down at my boots everywhere I went.I analysed my deeds, weigh my motives and eventually I cracked a code that could turn any of my deeds into filth. I cut my grandmothers wood to escape the guilt of not doing so, shy is a covert word for painfully vain, attempting not to be self indulgent IS self indulgent. There's no opposite to selfish it goes on and on. I hunted relentlessly for a noble or selfless deed that I could perform to elevate my value in the mirror. Only to discover that it was to caress my own vanity, to bolster my worth, to award myself with value.“Ohooo… Look how shiny and pristine I am!”“Bollocks!”“Well, there aren't any, not one, every single move I made was always aimed at some form of self gratification. I might pull a drowning stranger from the river to rescue myself from the horror of witnessing such distress, me me me, selfish selfish selfish... The word selfish can be removed from language, it has no antithesis, its a ruse, a con, a manipulation tool, it means... ...Sweet!... Fuck!... All!... Unless of course you’re going to perk up and prove me wrong but I really think you’d be wasting your time. In fact I’d be pretty disappointed if you even attempted.”“Dead?”“Fuck you Black, now who’s talking in riddles?”“And why did it take you seven years to turn up?”“I thought I'd give you a bit of time to catch the point.”“I could have done with a couple more years.”“To do what?”“To smoke backy and watch the sun go down.”“You don’t feel you missed something?”“Don’t you?” Kappa replied deadpan and with some spite.Kappa squirmed, Black was the Oracle, he didn’t imagine Black could miss a thing but was reluctant to see his point, reluctant to see what flavour of idiot he was this time around, reluctant to show that his bones were still rattling under his skin.Kappa, continuing his evasions, took a last deep draw on his smoke and stubbed it out on the grass.“How long will this journey take?”“Not sure about that Kappa.”Black tapped his pipe and put it away.The fire died unnaturally quickly and then sank into the earth leaving nothing but dark behind it.It shocks Kappa, the changes in this adventure are violent, Black is already on his feet and moving. Kappa, tired of feeling out of his depth, leaned against a tree in defiance and waited for his pupils to dilate. Black is nowhere to be seen by the time Kappa’s eyes had grown accustomed to the dark.“Nope, I’m going to take back a little control and say bon-voyage motherfucker, I’m going home.”The old chant echoed again in his mind.Kappa stepped across the clearing in the direction that they had come but found his exit barred with impenetrable bramble. He did a couple of laps of the clearing to make absolutely sure but it was no good. The only way out was the path that Black had taken.“This is impossible, this is all wrong, what the fuck is this shit!”But for the fire going out, Kappa would have stayed here, warm and light.“You’re a tricky fucker Black, if you jump out on me we’re going to fall fucking out!”Kappa reluctantly stepped back into the forest alone.Kappa felt further from home and more lost than he had ever been, he was less afraid of the dark and any stalking teeth than he was afraid that he might not find any quiet ever again, he wanted to be next to his fire.Even in the Rag n Bone man’s absence he still felt surrounded by something powerful, every branch, every leaf, the ground under his boots and the air that touched his face seemed to be connected to some force that was reaching out and touching him, probing at his existence. He was surrounded, hunted, it was inescapable, a rat in a shrinking drain pipe with a dog at each end.Kappa strode through the dark keeping a tight grip on his imagination until he caught the unmistakable smell of a coal fire “Fuck, we don’t want any of that fucking noise.” The unknown, unpredictable, uncontrollable shit coming at him, it meant people!Kappa stalked slowly upwind towards the source of the smell muttering insecurities to himself, “I tried all my life, I’m in for another bollocking, Ive tried to be decent… I am decent... am I decent?, where did I go wrong... am I wrong?”.“You're as wrong as fuck Kappa,” He whispers to himself.“Black wants you to know how wrong you are.”In the distance Kappa could hear voices, many voices. The sound stopped him in his tracks. “Shit, this could be worse than I thought.” Through the trees he could see slivers of light through shutters. I leave this noise to you in the hopes that if you find any utility in passing it along to any Drone, Builder or Hermit, you might do so to help them escape the mud a little quicker than I did or that it may keep them company along their way in their struggle home.Its difficult for me to assume the struggle is anything like a universal struggle that all humans face to some extent or other or that I can reach across into their struggle and inject any worthwhile optimism in their holding fast to the only thing that remains steadfast and survives the journey across the void (You hurt / I hurt)But that image in my head of me flying over my old boarding school and shouting down at the young me, some words of optimism about the terribly long journey he had in front of him, its stuck. I cant fly any more so I cant shout down to the poor aimless sucker pondering what the point of it all was but maybe we can shout down to someone grappling to make sense. I am pressed to place the three perspectives (“Chasing crows”, “The Spinnaker wind” and my ethics paper) into one book separated by two black pages indicating the split between the two sides of the door if I can make it make sense.Including these words here and the nod to the quality of Bens Mum.If I can get comfortable with how exposed they make me feel, I might try get a few copies printed off before I die so you can more easily play the Rag N Bone man to any other poor sucker you spot in the void.Love love love, The Sailor.PS: Don’t you dare speak that forbidden word to me though Dawn!The scar is still painful and I prefer to see with my own eyes if you have a muddy chick in your pocket, if you are one of those friendly fuckers that make the storms a little more adventure than harrowing :)In conclusion:The following paper is a more formal culmination of what survived the journey from insanity and back and the more robust construction that resulted.To many eyes, the “selfish” connotation is an offensive perspective that some folks recoil from in self-defence but I have yet to find an escape from its veracity or the beauty of it in action in the human animal.It has helped me a great deal over the years but has been kept under my hat to protect myself from inflicting upon others, what I see as true but they see as offensive or painful, the Rag n Bone man can only show you the door, the rest is up to us, folks are free to chase the crows if that’s their lesser of two evils, it is a safe harbour to gather their thoughts.I escaped from Drone to Sailor riding upon the veracity and potency of its value distinction and its ethical derivatives.Feel free to pick a higher quality method on your journey from child to old man, old women if you can find one, but please do find one and make it a friendly one :)I will place the paper here in lieu of somewhere better for it to survive my death.

Chasing Crows, very metaphorical. (Speaks to the child in us)The Spinnaker Wind, A little more exposed.(speaks to the adult)Then the paper below,(The raw scientist) cold, dry, hard to read, boring but potently makes clear what remains when the contortions are stripped away, When the Drone is dead and what little is left that is still breathing is the opposite of ugly or worthless and worth following where it leads us.Regarding authorship of this work, the fictional “Voight Kampff” machine detects the moral author inside us and the writer of these words is the scribe, the poor scholar attempting to follow its lead and write it down with as little error as is possible.I can only hope I did a reasonable job of doing so.AndI can only hope to be forgiven if I failed.-----------------------------------------------------------------------Agape-Centered Ethics: A Naturalistic Framework Grounded in Vicarious Aversion(Short Running Title): The ACE ModelMark Weatherill20 December 2025

 AbstractTraditional ethical theories struggle to locate universally accepted, objective sources for moral value, often relying on non-empirical axioms. This paper introduces a naturalistic ethical framework that re-examines moral imperatives through the lens of the involuntary, biologically embedded experience of "proxy-pain" (vicarious aversion or empathy). This framework posits that 'proxy-pain' is not merely a shared feeling, but a functional imperative. The agent’s drive for self-defense against this internal aversion creates a direct instruction to act, effectively transforming the descriptive 'is' of neurobiological distress into the prescriptive 'ought' of moral intervention. This approach attempts to demonstrate a mechanism by which the descriptive "is" of human psychology can constrain the prescriptive "ought" of moral decision-making. Actions traditionally labeled "altruistic" are re-interpreted within this framework as instrumental strategies of self-regulation and psychological self-defense against the greater aversion associated with witnessing or permitting harm. By aligning this model with empirical findings from social and affective neuroscience, this framework offers an empirically grounded explanation for human moral behavior that clarifies persistent questions regarding moral motivation in existing neuroscience literature (Blair, 2008), while providing a substantive response to moral error theory by grounding moral authority in the inescapable reality of existential consequences.

Keywords: altruism, aversion, empathy, ethics, is-ought problem, moral naturalism, philosophical psychology, "proxy-pain", self-defense. 

Public Significance StatementThe study suggests that human morality is not merely a social construct but a biological necessity for emotional self-regulation. By defining moral "oughts" as functional instructions to reduce the internal distress caused by seeing others suffer, this framework provides a new lens for understanding empathy-related disorders and improving social cooperation through objective, biological reality.

Traditional ethical systems, from deontology to utilitarianism, have long sought a stable, objective foundation for moral value. In their pursuit, philosophers often invoke abstract concepts such as "duty," "universalizability," or an intrinsic "greatest good"—concepts that typically lack an immediate basis in readily testable, empirical reality. Consequently, these theories often struggle to resolve fundamental questions concerning moral motivation and accountability, leaving a significant gap between philosophical theory and the empirical mechanisms of human behavior  (Greene, 2013, pp. 188–189, 289–292).

This paper proposes a naturalistic ethical framework that locates the source of moral value not in abstract reasoning, but in the pre-rational, involuntary human experience of empathy, reconceptualized here as "proxy-pain" (vicarious aversion). This model posits that the moral "ought" is a functional instruction to minimize this felt aversive experience within the moral agent, thereby offering a specific, mechanistic substrate that previous ethicists may have been gesturing toward with terms like agape, charity, and love.

The term “agape” is used strategically as a historical antecedent to draw attention to the trajectory of moral language. The argument is made that the original concept of agape was an attempt to define a condition where an individual's well-being becomes contingent upon the well-being of another; specifically, the experience of "You Hurt / I Hurt." However, as language is dynamic and meaning can drift, the introduction of precise terminology like "proxy-pain" is necessary to reclaim the required denotational clarity for empirical investigation. The study argues that this inherent capacity for vicarious aversion, deeply rooted in our neurobiology, serves as a fundamental mechanism that constrains moral behavior. This perspective suggests that morality is an emergent property of our neurobiology consistent with contemporary moral naturalism (Prinz, 2007).It is important to clarify that the Agape-Centered Ethics model is not an exercise in biological reductionism. Rather than attempting to simplify or dismiss the phenomenological complexity of moral experience, this framework acts as a foundational refinement. By identifying “proxy-pain” as the underlying mechanism, we provide an error-correcting algorithm that allows the agent to verify the validity of contemporary moral claims. This is not a constraint of moral scope, but a sharpening of the tools used to ascertain 'value facts,' making the profound experience of agape scientifically intelligible without stripping it of its social or psychological nuance. 

The Foundational Principles: Moral Realism and MechanismMoral action originates from an innate, involuntary physiological response to the actual or potential suffering of others. This response, rooted in the shared pain matrix of the brain, is not a conscious choice but a functional constraint on the agent’s experience providing the initial input for an algorithm for value facts. This provides the agent’s motivational state with a traceable origin, which can then be inspected against competing values for moral coherence. In this framework, 'coherence' is not merely an abstract logical consistency, but a homeostatic equilibrium: the agent rationalizes their choice by identifying which action minimizes the greatest projected total of aversive experience (“proxy-pain” or secondary social guilt) within their specific social and biological context.

Furthermore, this ethical approach re-frames moral failure. When an agent is overwhelmed by complexity, mistakes are categorized as an artifact of computational capacity or inability to sum (freeze) rather than an error of the core moral algorithm or malicious motive. The agent’s aversion minimization principle remains intact, allowing for rational self-correction and repair without existential damage to their moral identity."



The Neurobiological Registration of DistressEmpirical evidence confirms that the neural mechanisms for self-experienced and observed pain are significantly overlapping. Neuroimaging demonstrates that the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the insula are activated by the mere sight of pain in others (Decety & Jackson, 2004, p. 56). The insula’s role in monitoring the body’s physiological state suggests that witnessing distress in another is not a purely "representational" event; it is a somatic event for the observer. (Decety & Jackson 2006, p. 56) specify that while the self-perspective yields higher pain ratings, the neural network—including the parietal operculum and anterior insula—is fundamentally shared. This "proxy-pain" mechanism provides a functional bridge between first-person and third-person information.Furthermore, this aversion mechanism is modulated by specific neurochemicals. Research shows that the neuropeptide oxytocin (OXT) enhances feelings of guilt and shame specifically for intentional harm caused to others, and decreases the willingness to endorse such actions, providing a clear hormonal basis for the aversion mechanism (Zheng et al., 2024). This hormonal modulation suggests a complex, multi-layered biological system underlying moral emotions.



The Functional Is-Ought BridgeThe existence of this involuntary vicarious aversion provides a naturalistic basis for the relationship between the descriptive "is" (the neurobiological registration of distress) and the functional "ought" (the drive to alleviate that distress). In this framework, the moral imperative is understood as a homeostatic instruction: the agent ought to act to minimize the felt aversion within their total experiential field. By framing the "ought" as a functional requirement for psychological self-regulation, we sidestep the traditional naturalistic fallacy. Here, "ought" does not refer to a transcendent moral truth, but to a systemic necessity for an agent whose well-being is biologically contingent upon the state of the "other." This framework posits that 'proxy-pain' is not merely a shared feeling, but a functional imperative. The agent’s drive for self-defense against this internal aversion creates a direct instruction to act, effectively transforming the descriptive 'is' of neurobiological distress into the prescriptive 'ought' of moral intervention.

The Necessary Condition for Moral AgencyThe presence of this aversive mechanism is a necessary condition for typical human moral agency. The amoral individual—characterized by reduced amygdala functionality and empathy deficits—lacks this functional constraint. Research into psychopathy as a developmental disorder (Blair, 2008) highlights that this is an emotional pathophysiology rather than a failure of abstract reasoning. Critically, moral action requires both the involuntary signal of “proxy-pain” and the cognitive capacity for self-other distinction to regulate the response (Decety & Jackson, 2004). Without the initial aversive "trigger," the cognitive "regulation" has no signal to act upon.

Motivational Principles and the Epistemic Imperative

This section explores the homeostatic nature of altruism and provides the critical response to Richard Joyce’s Moral Error Theory.



The Motivational Principles: The Interdependent SelfThis section re-evaluates moral action as a form of homeostatic regulation for an interdependent agent. The model suggests that the traditional distinction between "self-interest" and "altruism" is a false dichotomy; both are driven by the same functional imperative: the minimization of aversive states.

The Aversion Minimization PrincipleAll deliberate actions are instrumental acts of self-regulation aimed at minimizing the agent's total aversive experience (e.g., physical pain, social guilt, or “proxy-pain”). Under this framework, "self-sacrificial" acts—such as a soldier shielding others—are interpreted as rational calculations where the aversion associated with inaction (witnessing harm or violating a core identity) is perceived as greater than the aversion of the sacrifice itself. The agent chooses the "lesser of two evils" in an act of psychological self-defense.

This is supported by research in comparative psychology. (Pozo et al., 2023, p. 1). demonstrate that helping behavior in rodents is modulated by internal states like hunger; when self-preservation demands are high, the capacity to respond to a conspecific’s distress decreases. This reinforces that moral action is not an abstract choice but is contingent upon competing homeostatic demands.

The Interdependent "Self"The "self" whose aversion is being minimized is intrinsically social. From an evolutionary perspective, "group defense" is a form of "self-defense." While the mechanism of “proxy-pain” is universal, its application is modulated by proximity and social bonding. This explains cross-cultural variability while maintaining a biological constant. Even non-human animals, such as canids and primates, exhibit behaviors resembling justice and consolation, suggesting a deeply conserved evolutionary basis for social concern that predates human abstract reasoning (Romero et al., 2010; Essler et al., 2017).While the mechanism of “proxy-pain” is universal, its application is modulated by proximity and social bonding. This modulation is often critiqued as an inherent bias or a "spotlight" that renders empathy an unreliable foundation for global ethics (Bloom, 2016). However, within the Agape-Centered framework, this discriminatory nature is not a 'bug' of the moral system, but a fundamental feature of value-fact identification. Without the neurobiological capacity to distinguish between higher and lower states of reciprocal utility—discriminating between the 'Rembrandt' and the 'snotty hanky' of social consequences—the moral agent would lack the necessary contrast to prioritize action. By acknowledging this 'spotlight' as a functional constraint, the model allows for the construction of ethical 'cheat sheets' that remain in lockstep with the agent's biological reality, rather than drifting into the cynicism of incoherent, abstract rules." 

The Epistemic Imperative: Clinical Truth vs. Narrative UtilityThis section addresses the tension between neurobiological reality and socially constructed narratives, engaging specifically with Richard Joyce’s (2001) Moral Error Theory.

The Myth of Categorical ReasonsRichard Joyce (2001) argues that since moral properties do not exist in the world, our moral talk is a "useful fiction." Joyce expresses concern that collapsing these fictions might cause social instability. This framework disagrees with Joyce’s "fictionalism" regarding transparency. We argue that the "authority" of morality does not need to be a fiction; it is grounded in the inescapable reality of existential consequences.

The Castaway AnalogyThe transition from a "subliminal" understanding of morality to an overt, naturalistic one is analogous to the resolution of complex psychological coping mechanisms. Consider a castaway who forms a deep connection with an inanimate object to mitigate the aversive agony of loneliness. In isolation, this fiction is a functional "lesser of two evils"—a necessary subterfuge to maintain psychological stability. However, the requirement to "let go" of the fiction arises when the agent returns to a world of actual "others."

While abandoning the simulated companion involves a painful loss, it is a natural release into a more robust state of being. Similarly, while humanity has long relied on the "useful fictions" of abstract moral axioms to manage social cooperation, the transition to an overt, naturalistic understanding represents an evolutionary "escape" from isolation. By moving into the reality of the biological "is," the agent moves from simulating value to participating in the authentic, functional mechanics of social interdependence. This suggests that fewer behavioral changes may occur than Joyce fears, as the agent is not losing morality, but simply trading a simulated companion for a real one. Recent analysis by Sinclair (2025) further challenges the necessity of these robust fictions, suggesting that moral discourse remains resilient even when grounded in naturalist or non-categorical terms.

Clinical Implications, Positionality, and References

This final section bridges the theory into psychological practice and provides the 2025 required reporting standards.



Academia and scientific institutions hold a primary imperative to prioritize clinical accuracy over narrative convenience. This requires that the underlying mechanisms of empathy and aversion be acknowledged as they are, not as they are socially performed. The utility of this transparency lies in promoting optimal social engagement. Overconfidence or under-confidence in an agent's self-valuation (their "value in the scrum") presents a detriment to the actual goal of balancing value facts in the human project at large. While overconfidence promotes stagnation of moral refinement, under-confidence fosters disengagement (withdrawal/anxiety). By aligning with an overt, naturalistic understanding, we move toward a robust state of rational self-governance that encourages accurate self-assessment, essential for a life worth living within a social reality. This indicates a more optimistic outlook on the human capacity for truth-seeking in the face of naturalistic reality.Reciprocal Utility as the Goal of Clinical TruthThe pursuit of a "life worth living" is fundamentally tied to an agent’s status as a valued member of the social scrum. While different agents provide varying utilities—ranging from diagnostic skill to physical strength or social skill—the attainment of a secure social position ("we need you and you need us") requires a strict adherence to the veracity of the moral algorithm. It is only through an accurate, non-fictional assessment of one's own value and the value of others that true reciprocal utility can be achieved. While “useful fictions” have historically facilitated social cohesion, the high-value state of being an essential part of the whole is most resilient when grounded in the veracity of the moral algorithm. Overt naturalistic transparency offers a robustness that fictions may lack, providing a stable mechanism for securing a seat in the human project—converting the "is" of biological reality into the "ought" of a life lived with meaning and social conviction.



Clinical and Theoretical ImplicationsThe proposed framework is useful for empirical sciences. It demands precision in moral terms. In psychological research, terms like "prosocial" often carry assumed moral weight. However, they lack explicit definitions. This ambiguity can cause errors. For example, "pure altruism" often disappears with a clear analysis of its motives.

Diagnostics and Personality PathologyThe “proxy-pain” model provides new ways to study personality disorders. Variations in vicarious aversion capacity may help to reformulate the differences between Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD) and Psychopathy. This model also provides a new framework for understanding Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD). Social value is linked to perceived "friendliness," a stand-in for agape. For people with SAD, their anxiety may show their empathetic sensitivity (“proxy-pain”).

The Deconstruction of "Pure Altruism"The difference between "pure altruism" often involves an unclear step from motive to action. This framework links Vicarious Aversion (Motive) to Homeostatic Regulation (Action). Removing the "selfless" motivation provides greater clarity in social psychology research.

Bridging Fact-Values with Relationship DynamicsThe "fact-values" in this model provide a solution to the "descriptive problem" in relationship psychology, specifically the work of Stanley et al. (2006). Their research on "sliding versus deciding" found that relationships formed via "sliding" (low deliberation) are less stable. This model resolves this by providing the moral mechanics needed for "deciding": using vicarious aversion as the metric for compatibility.

ConclusionThe Agape-Centered Ethics model asserts that the "ought" is intrinsically derived from the "is" of our shared neurobiology. We are moral agents laboring under a universal, involuntary mechanism that uses vicarious aversion to functionally project intrinsic value onto the well-being of others. However, the journey does not end at the biological registration of pain. By applying the algorithm for value facts, the agent moves from a state of isolated self-defense into a sophisticated state of reciprocal utility.

The pursuit of morality is thus revealed as an exercise in rational calculation and emotional honesty regarding this fundamental mechanism. By grounding moral motivation in objective neurobiology, we move beyond the "useful fictions" of the past and into an overt, clinical truth. This transition allows the agent to move from "simulating" value to "participating" in the authentic mechanics of social interdependence. Ultimately, the veracity of the algorithm is the very thing that secures the agent’s "seat at the table"—ensuring that our joint sum in the human project is significantly greater than the sum of our isolated parts. This framework provides fertile ground for future interdisciplinary research, offering an optimistic, empirically grounded response to the existential necessity of social belonging.



Positionality StatementThe author says this framework is informed by a personal journey of three decades. The work started from a struggle with internalizing moral "intuitions." This led to a search for "value facts" to navigate social interactions. The "Agape-Centered Ethics" model tries to ground value positions in a naturalistic logic.

CONTENTS:1. Chasing Crows: Written c. 2005. The metaphorical exploration of acute    existential collapse, isolation, and the scrupulosity loop.2. The Spinnaker Wind: Written c. 2025-2026. The real-world clearance of    the threshold. The transition from the log cabin back to the physical tarmac.3. Agape-Centered Ethics (The ACE Model): The naturalistic framework    grounded in vicarious aversion. The raw math behind the survival of the core.

CONTEXT:This archive represents a twenty-year error correction loop. It records the transition from Drone to Sailor using the unyielding invariant of the "You Hurt / I Hurt." The code is here for those who find themselves lost in the Big Empty and need a compass that requires no map. 

The temptation to further polish this scruffy, odd book has stalled against the idea that we might never, as humans, be out of the "Draft" phase in the Mandelbrot Set sense so "Draft=Finished" might be where I leave it."
